learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Somatosensory System.
Explain how the Somatosensory System contributes to sensation, regulation or behaviour.
Connect Somatosensory System function with clinically relevant symptoms.
Use lesion patterns and phenomenology cautiously rather than relying on one-to-one explanations.

anatomy.label: Peripheral receptors
anatomy.short: Detect mechanical, thermal and tissue-threat signals
anatomy.detail: Specialised endings translate physical events into neural firing.
anatomy.clinical: Peripheral injury changes both signal quantity and quality.

anatomy.label: Dorsal columns
anatomy.detail: Ascending fibres preserve detailed spatial information to the medulla.
anatomy.clinical: Lesions impair vibration and position sense ipsilaterally below the lesion.

anatomy.label: Anterolateral system
anatomy.detail: Fibres cross near spinal entry and ascend contralaterally.
anatomy.clinical: Lesions alter pain and temperature on the opposite side.

anatomy.label: Somatosensory thalamus
anatomy.detail: VPL and VPM nuclei route body and facial information to cortex.
anatomy.clinical: Thalamic lesions may cause sensory loss or central pain.

anatomy.label: Somatosensory cortex
anatomy.detail: S1 represents body regions somatotopically; association areas integrate body schema.
anatomy.clinical: Cortical lesions can impair localisation, recognition or awareness.
